item.title: Version 0.2.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • Launch commands defined as aliases or functions in ~/.zshrc (or ~/.bashrc) are no longer reported as "not installed". VSVibe now asks your interactive shell, and a shell that takes too long to answer never causes a false warning.
  • Token usage is shown per pane: each pane follows its own Claude conversation, so two panes in one project no longer show the same numbers, and a conversation run with another alias or account is counted correctly. The numbers switch to the new conversation after /clear.

Added

  • When a project's launch command is a shell alias for another Claude account (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=…), the project editor says so and offers Register, which adds it as a VSVibe alias and installs its hooks in one click.
  • Aliases & Claude Hooks… lists project launch commands that aren't registered yet, with the Claude account each one uses and a Register button.
  • On launch, VSVibe offers to install or update the Claude hooks when they are missing or outdated (notifications and session restore need them), with Not Now and Don't Ask Again.

Changed

  • The hook status flags a registered alias whose Claude config folder doesn't exist yet, or that Claude Code hasn't used yet, and tells you to run that command once and log in. Installing hooks for such an alias creates the folder and its settings.json, which Claude Code reads on first run.

item.title: Version 0.2.0
item.description:
Added

  • Automatic updates (Sparkle 2): VSVibe checks for new versions in the background, shows the release notes and offers Install Update, Remind Me Later or Skip This Version. "Check for Updates…" is in the app menu, and the new Settings window has an Updates tab to turn automatic checks and automatic downloads on or off.
  • Session restore: open panes come back after the app relaunches (on by default, can be turned off in Settings). When it is off, installing an update asks before closing running sessions. Each Claude pane resumes its own conversation with the alias (Claude config dir / account) that ran it; click Update Hooks in Aliases & Claude Hooks… once after updating.
  • Developer ID signed, notarized release DMGs published on GitHub Releases.

Changed

  • Strict quality gates: every SwiftLint rule, compiler warnings as errors, at least 90% unit-test coverage of the core logic, unused-code checks (Periphery) and a SonarQube quality gate, all enforced in CI.
